subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw add `bindings[].tools.allow/deny` as a supported route/ACP security boundary, and what precedence should it have relative to existing tool-policy layers?
rationale: The request adds a new public config and security-control surface across routing, ACP bindings, and tool execution; automation cannot safely choose that authorization contract or precedence.

options.title: Design Binding-Scoped Policy
options.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Use Existing Policy Surfaces
options.body: Decline the new binding key and document group, sender, session, and per-agent policy as the supported way to restrict tools.

options.title: Defer To Broader Identity Work
options.body: Block this narrower feature on the broader scoped session or conversation identity design if maintainers want one authorization model instead of binding-specific policy.

recommendation.title: Design Binding-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and approve an end-to-end binding policy contract with precedence, enforcement, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent history on scoped conversation capability profiles and central policy/routing work adjacent to this security-boundary decision.
